summary: Artemis is a web page developed to solve the challenge of Identifying Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars. An important note, Artemis only solves de challenge for the Moon, Mars was left out of the scope. The goal for Artemis is that it can be used by amateurs to look around and play, also be used by scientist and workers to find places were they can do research and test new technology.
details:
Artemis is an interactive application that uses scientific maps of the Moon and Earth to identify terrestrial locations with characteristics similar to those found on the lunar surface. When users select a location on the Moon, Artemis analyzes its environmental and geological properties and searches for comparable locations on Earth. Users can customize the importance of different factors, explore ranked results, view satellite imagery of each location, and understand which measurements contributed to its similarity score.

We expanded the lunar analysis by integrating seven scientific measurements: elevation, slope, roughness, rock abundance, bolometric temperature, regolith temperature, and hydrogen abundance. Using NASA datasets from LOLA, Diviner, and Lunar Prospector, Artemis can analyze all six Apollo landing sites or any user-selected lunar coordinates.

For Earth comparisons, we incorporated NASA MODIS, ERA5-Land, and SoilGrids, providing nighttime land surface temperature, soil temperature, and coarse soil fragment measurements. Users can select and weight four similarity criteria: slope, roughness, bolometric temperature, and regolith temperature. The application displays individual similarity percentages, original measurements from both locations, and an overall weighted score. Missing measurements are handled without treating them as zero, while additional scientific variables remain available as contextual information.

The frontend was developed using React and TypeScript, with interactive 3D representations of the Moon and Earth rendered through globe.gl and imagery provided by NASA. The backend was built in Python, using scientific data processing tools to handle large geospatial datasets. To improve performance and reduce memory requirements, Earth data stored in Parquet files is extracted into separate binary columns and accessed through memory mapping, allowing efficient searches across approximately 82 million terrestrial points.

Artemis also includes a local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows users to explore and refine Earth analog searches using natural language. Built with Node.js, the MCP SDK, and Zod, it communicates with a persistent Python search worker. The buscar tool processes scientific criteria, configurable weights, and mission presets without inventing measurements. Search results are saved in data/earth/shortlist.json, with up to eight candidates returned to the language model and the complete results sent to the map through Server-Sent Events (SSE).

The MCP supports two explanation styles: professional, which provides technical terminology and numerical differences, and amateur, which explains results in more accessible language. Both use the same underlying measurements and scores. Additional tools allow users to apply geographical and scientific filters, restore hidden candidates, review filtered results, and revisit previous searches without recalculating the entire Earth dataset.

To keep searches efficient, Artemis initially selects up to 50 terrestrial candidates using terrain slope and roughness, then incorporates available temperature measurements to refine their ranking according to user-defined weights. The system preserves data provenance, reports missing values and coverage, and distinguishes exploratory comparisons from direct scientific equivalence.

By combining planetary datasets, interactive visualization, customizable similarity searches, and natural-language exploration, Artemis makes scientific information more accessible and helps identify potential Earth analog environments for lunar exploration, technology testing, and future mission preparation.
